> Hello,
>
> I already posted about this issue, that I still experiment.
> I'll try to be as clear as possible, and I have an example package on
> github to help reproducing the problem.
>
> Description: I can not make statET to index newer installed versions of a
> package using "R environment -->  Index changes" action, knowing the
> official version string of the package (from the DESCRIPTION file) has not
> changed.
>
> Why do I need this ? We work on packages on a daily basis and use
> continuous integration.
> We can not increase the version number of the package for each
> modification. Still, we'd like to have the new content of the help
> documentation.
>
> Overview of the example:
> I will install a version of package rikiki with FOO1 as description of
> entry foo.
> Then have statET index this package, and display help(foo).
> Then install a newer version of the package with FOO2 as description of
> entry foo.
> At this point, I can not have statET display the new version of help(foo).
>
> Steps to reproduce:
>
> # get the package
> git clone https://github.com/kforner/rikiki.git
> # make a temp directory to install the package in
> mkdir lib
> cd rikiki
>
>
> # ======= install the version foo1 of the package =================
> # run inside statET a R console and set the current directory inside rikiki
> # remove the current foo.Rd if any
> if (file.exists('man/foo.Rd')) file.remove('man/foo.Rd')
> # copy foo.Rd Version 1
> file.copy('foo1.Rd', 'man/foo.Rd')
> # install the package in temp dir
> system("R CMD INSTALL -l ../lib/ .", intern=TRUE)
> # put the temp lib dir in the lib paths to that statET can see it
> .libPaths(c(.libPaths(), '../lib'))
> # load the package
> library(rikiki, lib = '../lib')
>
> # ask for help
> help(foo)
> # nothing AS EXPECTED
>
> Now, in the Console view, select "R environment -->  Index changes"
> The indexing process should find the new package, and index it.
>
> help(foo)
> # ==> display FOO1 AS EXPECTED
>
> So far so good.
>
> # ======= install the version foo1 of the package =================
> # remove the current foo.Rd if any
> if (file.exists('man/foo.Rd')) file.remove('man/foo.Rd')
> # copy foo.Rd Version 2
> file.copy('foo2.Rd', 'man/foo.Rd')
> # install the package in temp dir
> system("R CMD INSTALL -l ../lib/ .", intern=TRUE)
>
>
> Now, in the Console view, select "R environment -->  Index changes"
> The indexing process does not seem find the new package (too fast).
>
> Now start a NEW StatET R console
> library(rikiki, lib = '../lib')
> help(foo)
> # ==> display FOO1 instead of FOO2
>
> Ultimate check:
> *start a standard R console (not statET)*
> library(rikiki, lib = '../lib')
> help(foo)
> # ==> display FOO2 as expected.
>
>
> Probable cause:
> in de.walware.statet.r.internal.core.rhelp.REnvIndexChecker.::checkPackage
>
> I noticed (line 160):
>         else if (!packageHelp.getVersion().equals(pkgVersion)) {
>
> meaning that the package is ignored if a same pkgVersion of the package
> has already been indexed.
>
> A possible fix would be to store the date of the DESCRIPTION file for
> instance, and to compare them.
>
>
The 'Date' field of the DESCRIPTION file will not help (it is user
specified),
but it may be possible to use the information from the 'Built' field which
is
updated each time you install the package

Best,

messages.subject: Intel MKL libraries with remote StatET connection crashes R?
messages.subject_clean: Intel MKL libraries with remote StatET connection crashes R?
messages.body_plain:
Is anyone using the Intel MKL math libraries with StatET connecting to a 
remote R server?

I am trying to connect to R 2.15.3 running on Linux from a Windows box 
running Eclipse 3.8.2 and StatET (Java Core 1.1.3, Eclient 1.2.1).  Have 
been using this setup for months without issue.  We recently recompiled 
R with the Intel MKL optimized numeric libraries, and are running into 
problems, but only through StatET.

If I run a simple matrix operation like "crossprod(1:4)" in a local R 
session on the server, it returns fine.  On a more complex operation, it 
is noticeably faster (one test went from 86 seconds down to 35 seconds), 
which is what we were hoping to see by using these libraries.

But if I start a remote session via Eclipse/StatET, and run the same 
command, it kills the entire remote R session.  In the log files on the 
server I see the error"Intel MKL FATAL ERROR: Cannot load libmkl_mc3.so 
or libmkl_def.so".  I've compared LD_LIBRARY_PATH in both the local and 
remote sessions, and can't find any differences -- both have entries 
pointing to the Intel MKL directories.

I've fiddled with numerous settings and environment variables, tried 
reinstalling rj and rj.gd, without success.  I don't know if this is a 
StatET problem, an Intel MKL problem, or a local configuration problem, 
but since it works when run locally without StatET involved, I wanted to 
ask the list whether anyone else has this kind of configuration working?

Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Keith

I had previously tried reinstalling the StatET plugin but that didn't work.
You inspired me to try and dig a bit deeper, and I got my StatET to work
again.

Help -> About Eclipse -> Installation Details

console now works again.

Thanks,
Greg

After the conversion using svn2git, you can (for example) in 
Eclipse/StatET switch to the 'Git' perspective and in the
'Git Repositories' view:
  - Add your local repo, so you can easily manage it using EGit
  - Change the branch using 'Switch To' in the context menu,
    if required
  - Select the 'Working Directory' or a subfolder which, you want
    to use as Eclipse project, and start 'Import Projects...' from
    the context menu. It allows you to import existing project (if the
    .project file is still present) or also to setup a new project
    (so you can configure it as R project).
